h1:
Prachuap in 3 Days, 2 Nights
Hua Hin–Khao Sam Roi Yot–Prachuap Town
intro: Prachuap Khiri Khan is a very long province, stretching from Hua Hin in the north all the way down to the narrowest part of Thailand in the south. If you have 3 days and 2 nights, the cleanest way to do it is top to bottom: start in Hua Hin on day one, stop at Khao Sam Roi Yot along the way, then spend the night in Prachuap town. This plan is an easy self-drive with no rush, and it packs in beaches, a cave, mountain views, and plenty of local food.

blocks.html: Hua Hin is about 230 km from Bangkok, roughly a 3.5-hour drive, and Prachuap town is another 90 km or so further south. This plan works best if you drive yourself, because the sights are spread out and public transport between them is hard to piece together, especially around Khao Sam Roi Yot. If you really don't have a car, rent one in Hua Hin, or take the train down to Hua Hin and rent from there.

We've laid out the route heading steadily south so you never double back. Day one is all Hua Hin. Day two tackles Khao Sam Roi Yot in the morning, then moves into Prachuap town. Day three covers Prachuap town before you head home.

blocks.label: Day 1
blocks.title: Hua Hin — beach, market, and the legendary train station

items.activity: Leave Bangkok early, reach Hua Hin by late morning, and drop your bags at the hotel
items.note: Setting off before 7 am helps you dodge the traffic around Rama II Road

items.activity: Stop for photos at Hua Hin Railway Station, a cream-and-red wooden building with the King Rama VI royal pavilion — one of the prettiest stations in Thailand
items.note: Free to enter, but it gets crowded late morning, so come earlier if you want clear shots

items.activity: Have lunch around Chatchai Market, the old morning market in the town center, with fresh produce, dried seafood, salted fish, and souvenirs
items.note: Most breakfast and lunch spots in central Hua Hin close in the early afternoon

items.activity: Swim or just relax at Hua Hin Beach, or drive over toward Khao Takiab, which has plenty of beachfront cafes and photo spots
items.note: At low tide you can walk far out on Hua Hin Beach, which is great for evening photos

items.activity: Wander the Hua Hin Night Market, packed with street food and grilled seafood, open roughly 6 pm to midnight
items.note: Seafood stalls in the market run a bit pricey, so check prices before you order to be safe

blocks.title: Where to stay the first night
blocks.html: Pick a place around central Hua Hin or Khao Takiab so the market and beach are an easy walk away, and you can get an early start toward Khao Sam Roi Yot the next morning.

blocks.label: Day 2
blocks.title: Khao Sam Roi Yot — Phraya Nakhon Cave, then into Prachuap town

items.activity: Check out and leave Hua Hin for Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park, about an hour's drive through Pranburi
items.note: Fill up on fuel and grab drinking water before entering the park, since shops inside are few

items.activity: Hike up to Phraya Nakhon Cave. The highlight is the Kuha Karuhas royal pavilion, where a shaft of sunlight pours through the cave's opening in the late morning
items.note: The cave is open 08:30–15:00. Entry is 40 THB for Thai adults, 20 THB for children, and 200/100 THB for foreigners

items.activity: The way up involves a short but fairly steep climb, around 30–45 minutes on foot, or you can take a boat from Bang Pu Beach and come up via Laem Sala Beach
items.note: Wear sneakers. The light is best around 10:00–10:30, so don't arrive too late or you'll miss it

items.activity: Come down from the cave and eat around Bang Pu or Sam Roi Yot, where there are local seafood spots at reasonable prices
items.note: This area is known for fresh prawns, shellfish, and crab thanks to the coast and nearby farms

items.activity: Drive south into Prachuap town, about an hour, and check in at a hotel in town
items.note: Prachuap town is much smaller than Hua Hin, so hotels and restaurants are all close together

items.activity: Stroll along Prachuap Bay, watch the Saran Withi Bridge at sunset, then find dinner in town
items.note: Prachuap town is known for mackerel and seafood — ask locals to point you to the good spots

blocks.title: Check before you go to Khao Sam Roi Yot
blocks.html: During the rainy season or at high tide, the boat route and walking trail can close on some days. Check the Khao Sam Roi Yot National Park page before you set off to be sure.

blocks.label: Day 3
blocks.title: Prachuap town — Khao Chong Krachok and Ao Manao before heading home

items.activity: Have breakfast in town, then climb Khao Chong Krachok, the town's landmark, up its 396 steps
items.note: Khao Chong Krachok is open 05:00–20:00 and has lots of monkeys — watch anything in your hands and any food bags

items.activity: Reach the temple at the summit of Khao Chong Krachok for 360-degree views over all three bays — Ao Noi, Ao Prachuap, and Ao Manao
items.note: Going up early means gentler sun, open views, and good photos

items.activity: Drive to Ao Manao, a quiet white-sand beach inside the Wing 5 air base, and stop at the World War II heroes memorial
items.note: This is a military zone, so you'll exchange your ID for a pass at the entrance and should dress modestly

items.activity: Have a farewell lunch in Prachuap town — try the fresh mackerel or seafood before you head back
items.note: You can pick up salted mackerel, shrimp paste, and dried seafood as souvenirs at the town market

items.activity: Set off back to Bangkok, stopping along the way to buy Prachuap's famous pineapples by the roadside on Phetkasem Road
items.note: Prachuap pineapples are sweet and juicy and cheaper than buying in town — pick ones with fresh green leaves

items: 2 nights' accommodation — a mid-range hotel in Hua Hin/Prachuap runs about ฿900–1,800 per night, which works out to roughly ฿900–1,800 per person for the whole trip when shared between two
Phraya Nakhon Cave park entry — 40 THB for Thais (200 THB for foreigners)
Food — around ฿200–400 per meal, with seafood cheaper than in Bangkok
Fuel + tolls — about ฿1,500–2,000 per car for the Bangkok–Prachuap round trip

blocks.text: Tips to make the plan work

items.name: When to go
items.blurb: November to February brings good weather and little rain, ideal for caving and climbing. In the rainy season the sea turns murky and some trails get slippery

items.name: Self-drive is best value
items.blurb: The sights are spread out and public transport is hard to connect, so driving yourself is far more flexible. No car? Rent one in Hua Hin

items.name: Leave time for the cave
items.blurb: Phraya Nakhon Cave means a climb and timing the light, so don't pack day two too tightly

faq.q: Is 3 days and 2 nights enough for Prachuap?
faq.a: It's enough for the three main areas — Hua Hin, Khao Sam Roi Yot, and Prachuap town. If you also want to reach Ban Krut, Bang Saphan, or further south, allow 4–5 days, because the province is very long and the districts are roughly an hour's drive apart.

faq.q: Is the hike to Phraya Nakhon Cave hard, and how much is entry?
faq.a: There's a short but fairly steep climb, around 30–45 minutes on foot, or you can take a boat from Bang Pu Beach and come up via Laem Sala Beach. Park entry is 40 THB for Thai adults and 20 THB for children, and the cave is open 08:30–15:00.

faq.q: What time should I arrive at Khao Sam Roi Yot to catch the light in the cave?
faq.a: The shaft of sunlight pouring through the cave onto the Kuha Karuhas pavilion is at its best around 10:00–10:30. Aim to enter the cave when it opens at 08:30 so you have time to climb up and catch the light just right.

faq.q: Can I do this plan without my own car?
faq.a: You can, but it's awkward, because the sights are spread out and public transport is hard to connect, especially around Khao Sam Roi Yot. The easiest way is to take the train or a minivan down to Hua Hin, then rent or charter a car for Khao Sam Roi Yot and Prachuap town.

faq.q: What are the best souvenirs from Prachuap town?
faq.a: Prachuap's sweet, juicy pineapples are sold along Phetkasem Road, while mackerel, salted fish, shrimp paste, and dried seafood are easy to find at the town market — and cheaper than buying in Bangkok.
